title: How Many Squares?
summary: Count in a fixed order, one size at a time.

steps.title: The puzzle
sentences: Picture a big square made of a 3 by 3 grid of small squares, like a noughts and crosses board.
How many squares of any size can you find?
points: Picture a big square made of a 3 by 3 grid of small squares, like a noughts and crosses board.

steps.title: How to think about it
sentences: Count the squares of each size one at a time.

steps.title: The method: Count by size
sentences: Squares of size 1 by 1: there are 9.
Squares of size 2 by 2: there are 4, because a 2 by 2 square can start in 2 places across and 2 places down.
Squares of size 3 by 3: there is just 1.
points: Squares of size 1 by 1: there are 9.

steps.title: The answer
sentences: For a 4 by 4 grid the same method gives 16 plus 9 plus 4 plus 1, which is 30.
Counting in an order stops you missing any or counting twice.

quiz.q: How many squares in a 2 by 2 grid?
quiz.why: Four small squares and one big one, so 5.
